title: Republicans Defend Swing Seats in Arizona Amid Competitive Primaries
text:
Arizonas 1st and 2nd Congressional Districts are key battLegrounds in the 2024 elections, with Republicans facing stiff competition from Democrats in both districts. The 1st District is open after Rep. David Schweikert (R-AZ) ran for governor, while the 2nd District is represented by Rep. Eli Crane, who faces a rematch against former Navajo Nation President Jonathan Nez.
Republicans are defending two swing seats in Arizona , including the open 1st Congressional District, which is open after incumbent Rep. David Schweikert (R-AZ) ran for governor.
Collins absent from Trump's Georgia rally as Home votes keep him in DC. Arizona's 2nd District, currently represented by Republican Rep. Eli Crane, is a greater reach for Democrats but is targeted by the 1st Congressional District: Jay Feely vs. Amish Shah. Republican Jay Feely and Democrat Amish Shah are both vying for this Scottsdale-based district after Schweikert bowed out of the race.
That left the rAce open for Feely, a former NFL kicker and broadcaster for CBS. The Trump-endorsed athlete fended off a primary challenge from former Arizona state Rep. Joseph Chaplik. Feely will proceed to the general election with 49.8% of his party's primary vote.
Democrats as well held a competitive primary for the district. Shah,a former state representative who narrowly lost to Schweikert in 2024, once again aimed to appear on the November ballot.
Shah defeated Marlene Galan-Woods, an establishment-backed former broadcast journalist, by roughly 6 percentage points. the DCCC spent roughly $500,000 on joint ads with Galan-Woods, according to nonpartisan firm AdImpact,while other outside groups spent nearly $3 million supporting her. crane will once again face former Navajo Nation President Jonathan Nez in this vast district, which stretches from Flagstaff and Prescott to just south of Phoenix and includes 12 Native American reservations. Nez, meanwhile,has a strong base of support in the district's Native American communities.
The district includes large swaths of reservation land. One in five residents is Native American, according to Arizona Both candidates advanced on Tuesday night in uncontested primaries. Nez and Crane have proven to be apt fundraisers, meaning this race could become costly despite currently flying under the radar. The matchup will be a reprisal of their 2024 contest, when Crane bested Nez by 9 points.
Vice President Kamala Harris lost the district by 15 points. Rep. Juan Ciscomani (R-AZ) and Marine veteran JoAnna Mendoza are headed for a duel of their own in this toss-up district, home of the iconic gunfight at the OK Corral in Tombstone. The district, which includes Tucson's northern suburbs and a small section of the U.S.-Mexico border, is one of the most competitive seats in the country.
Trump endorsed Ciscomani in his race against Mendoza, a political newcomer and former drill instructor. Trump carried the district by less than 1 point in 2024 after the GOP narrowly lost the seat in 2020
